Hi Lina / SecurityOps team —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps focused on the networking choices (PrivateLink vs VPC peering) and IP allowlist approach so we can scope Dedicated vs Private deployment correctly.

Key notes from the conversation:
- AcmeCorp requirement: customer traffic and logs must remain inside your VPC; no public internet egress for model payloads.
- Preferred options discussed: AWS PrivateLink endpoint for hosted-control-plane connectivity OR VPC peering for fully private deployments (Private on-prem / VPC-hosted).
- Procurement signal: you may need a signed SOW + security addendum before we spin up dedicated capacity.

Action items (owner / ETA):
1) Acme: confirm which AWS account(s) we should expect endpoints from and whether a cross-account role is acceptable (Lina) / by 2026-03-03
2) Redwood: share standard PVPC networking checklist + sample endpoint config (Monica / today) — attached: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx
3) Redwood SE: provide recommended CIDR ranges, NAT/route considerations, and PrivateLink service name for our endpoint (Rishi / 2026-03-01)
4) Procurement: we'll target a preliminary SOW for sign-off; Monica to send draft (Monica / 2026-03-02)

Technical notes we promised to surface in follow-up:
- PrivateLink advantages: no route table changes in Acme VPC, simplified security posture, recommended for orgs that disallow peering across accounts.
- VPC peering advantages: lower latency, more control over routing; requires tighter route-table and corporate firewall work.

I've attached our initial network diagram (acme_private_vpc_diagram_v1.pdf) and the checklist for your network team. Rishi / Neha are cc'd for technical follow-up.

Thanks, Monica — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from SecurityOps and infra:

1) PrivateLink vs Peering: Our security team leans toward PrivateLink because it avoids adding routes to our core VPC. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for the control plane and whether data plane traffic (model payloads) would traverse that endpoint or still go over public IPs?

2) IP allowlist: We need to lock down egress to a short list of IPs/ranges. Can you provide the exact IP ranges Redwood will use (or confirm that you can support customer-provided NATs so we only see our own static IPs)?

3) Cross-account access: Will setting up PrivateLink require us to create an acceptance step in the console, or can Redwood initiate a cross-account role? Our infra prefers that we accept endpoints from partners rather than granting broad roles.

4) Timing / SOW: Procurement wants to understand how long it will take from signed SOW to a working PVPC endpoint (ballpark).

If you can loop in the SEs with specifics, we'll validate with infra and get back.

Thanks,

Hi Lina —

Quick technical answers inline for your infra/security team: 

1) PrivateLink support: Yes — Redwood supports AWS Interface VPC Endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for the control plane and for model inference traffic (data plane) when you choose our Hosted-with-PVPC option. That means traffic between your VPC and our endpoint stays on the AWS network (no public internet hop). You will see our endpoint service name (com.amazonaws.vpce.svc-xxxx) which you accept in your account; acceptance is a console/API action on your side.

2) IP allowlist options: two supported patterns:
  a) Customer-managed NAT: Your VPC routes egress through your NAT gateway. All outbound appear from your static NAT IPs — we accept connections from your VPC to our endpoint; Redwood does not require a fixed outbound IP block in this mode.
  b) Redwood-managed egress (when using VPC peering or dedicated private subnet): we can publish a set of CIDR ranges for our egress. For Hosted-with-PVPC we recommend PrivateLink so no external IPs are required; for Dedicated/Dedicated-Private we can provide static egress IP ranges upon request (we'll share them in the SOW).

3) Cross-account roles / acceptance: PrivateLink requires that you accept the VPC Endpoint Service from your account. Redwood will create a service and provide the service name; your infra will create an interface endpoint and accept. No cross-account role is strictly required. If you want Redwood to provision on your behalf, we can do it with a short-lived cross-account provisioning role—but we understand that many customers prefer to manually accept.

4) Timing: Typical timeline from signed SOW to working endpoint: ~5-10 business days for Hosted-with-PVPC (PrivateLink) assuming security review completes and Acme provides account details. For Dedicated private clusters with peering/on-prem integrations, plan 2-4 weeks depending on procurement and firewall changes. We'll include exact timelines in SOW.

Minimum info we need from Acme to proceed:
- AWS account ID(s) for endpoint creation
- VPC and subnet IDs where you want the interface endpoint (or peering candidate CIDR)
- Any proxy/NAT constraints or mandatory egress IPs

I've attached a simple network diagram and checklist for your infra team to review. Happy to jump on a 30-min technical call with your infra to walk through the endpoint acceptance flow.

Regards,
